crop_processing.coordinates: Original image pixels, exact frozen boxes
crop_processing.rotation_method: B17 only: PIL rotate(-40), BICUBIC, expand=True, white fill, before enlargement

boxes.comments: Opening parenthesis, que, la, and section are complete. The final sign has an open upper cup, two raised outer tips, and a central descending stem; read psi from that outline. No following clipped word is supplied.

Both E forms have curved upper and lower lobes. The first lower U has an open entry and a long right stem. Its tiny nested index has a low arch and a slightly lowered right leg; eta/n remains local. The final K has a stem and separated diagonal branches. No punctuation is supplied.
Three connected small s-shaped bodies are visible. No period follows them within the complete central group; the abbreviation is left unexpanded.
The whole morphique and the closing parenthesis are visible. The p and q descenders, h ascender, and i dot support the letter sequence. No terminal stop is added.
The apostrophe is separate. The long stroke returning left beneath the word is the g descender; it is not separately encoded as an underline.

Théorème and a small separate terminal point are readable; the single underline extends under that point. A compact following label is heavily crossed by several oblique strokes and cannot be recovered as a number. Its estimated one-glyph extent is marked deleted and illegible. A question-mark-like curve with a lower point overlaps the right edge of that cluster and is uncertain; the far-right closing parenthesis is clear. No opening parenthesis is supplied. The boundary between cancellation and question mark remains uncertain.

Soit is readable. The following glyph combines a long top bar and central vertical with an S-like upper curve and lower return. T/S is preserved as an overlapping-form doubt; no revision chronology is assigned.
The explicit hyphen separates anneau and jauge. The closing parenthesis and following comma are retained. The comma approaches the right edge. Preceding clipped material is excluded.
The T has a long top stroke and a vertical stem. Its following comma descends distinctly. On begins with a large O and ends in a compressed low n. Lower neighboring-line fragments are excluded.

Full central formula row read. The first argument separator has an upper point and a lower comma, read semicolon. Each pi has a lower 1. U entries are open; the second U is tilded. The second formula has K, barred K, a wavy-over-straight two-level relation, and Gal with barred K slash K. Curved E forms are rendered mathcal here. Adjacent clipped lines are excluded.

The complete central formula starts with an unsubscripted pi, two equality bars, then pi with lower 1. The first U carries a lower barred K and the second a tilde. A separate terminal point follows the closing parenthesis. The neighboring word par has a clipped p descender and is excluded from the formula reading.

The baseline Considérons and following short word are crossed by a long rising cancellation stroke; the second word remains uncertain under it. On a donc is raised above the canceled baseline, with a curved attachment dropping into the canceled area. The d ascender in donc meets the upper crop edge, while the word bodies are readable. No punctuation or further word is supplied.

The upper live line reads un carre/cartésien de groupes profinis; the accent of carré is not isolated securely. Below it, section is obscured by a separate darker strike and remains uncertain. A longer rising strike crosses pt K-rationnel de U_K. No abbreviation stop is securely isolated after pt. The final comma lies below and to the right of the strike endpoint and is encoded outside deletion. Neighboring formula fragments at the upper and lower edges are excluded. The first image display was truncated; the same saved crop was reopened and actually inspected before this return.

The d ascender, apostrophe, low o/u bodies, and grave accent support d'où. A long stroke runs along and through the lower word bodies, ending in the dense right cluster. Its role as cancellation versus a live low joining/underlining stroke remains unresolved and is marked locally.

All four nodes, both ends of all four connectors, and the equality with Gal are included. Each horizontal connector has one left-pointing head; thick or looped right endpoints are retained as shaft endpoints. Both vertical connectors end downward; the right terminal head is small and loop-like. Four surj labels are present, without supplied periods: top above, left to the left, right to the right, bottom below. The upper-right nested index and lower-right index have arch-like joined forms whose eta/K reading remains unresolved. The open U entries, lower-left S, bar over the first K in Gal, slash, and final closing parenthesis are visible. A fragment of the canceled line at the top edge is excluded.
The central word has a descending p stem, a tall l return, a low u body, and terminal s curl, read plus. Right-edge neighboring letters and the clipped upper stroke are excluded.

Margin note rotated clockwise 40 degrees for inspection. The star and the eight successive lines are included. The low dim group is partly crossed by the descender from que and remains uncertain. A first accent in élémentaire is visible; the second accent cannot be isolated securely and is marked locally. The numeral 1, both numerical pairs with comma separators, i.e., pi with lower 1, and nul are retained. No final period is added. Main-body fragments along the rotated right boundary and beneath the note are excluded; their clipped words are not completed.
Separate small lower-left foliation: a crossed 7 followed by a two-lobed 3. Encoded as a margin number.

The complete word anabélien is followed by a raised six-rayed star and a separate descending comma. The star is retained at the upper-right of the word as a reference sign; no phrase beyond the crop is added.
